title: Agentic Harness — Feature List
description: Mandatory per D-2. Every new feature (schema_version v3) carries `dev/<feature>/feature-list.json` conforming to this schema. Each entry declares one observable behavior plus the shell command whose exit code determines pass/fail. Finalize blocks until every entry has status=passed. Paths in verification_command are repo-root-relative per D-11; the orchestrator runs them from `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`. Scale-down rule (1-entry feature-list) is documented in plan.template.md §Feature list and only satisfies this schema when all four conditions in that rule hold.

schema_note.description: Free-form note about the list's scope, conventions, or cwd assumptions. Not load-bearing; orchestrator ignores it.

features.description: Ordered list of granular pass/fail assertions. Order is not semantically significant; `id` is the stable key.

id.description: Stable feature identifier. Format: F-NNN where NNN is a zero-padded integer (e.g. F-001, F-042). Must be unique within the list.

description.description: One-line statement of the observable pass condition. Present tense, concrete, grep-friendly.

verification_command.description: Shell command whose exit code determines pass/fail. Paths are repo-root-relative per D-11; orchestrator prefixes `cd $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && ` at evaluation time. Exit code 0 flips status to `passed`; any non-zero exit leaves status unchanged.

status.description: Current evaluation state. `pending` before first run, `in_progress` while the blocking phase is active, `passed` once verification_command returned 0, `blocked` when a dependency or environment issue prevents evaluation. Finalize requires `passed` for every entry.

status_reason.description: Optional free-text explanation when status is `blocked` or `in_progress`. Example: `awaiting_human_unity_verification`.

passed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp captured the moment status flipped to `passed`. Null while status is not `passed`.

blocking_phase.description: The phase expected to complete this feature. Format: phase-N (e.g. phase-1, phase-10). Used by the orchestrator to attribute feature progress to the responsible phase and to surface regressions when a later phase breaks an earlier feature.
